conventions.convention: Assume Countable Choice for the Hilbert-space and completed Fock constructions.

The inertial metric is diag(−1,1,1,1), while the gamma matrices satisfy {γᵃ,γᵇ}=−2ηᵃᵇI. Coordinates have length units; μ, momentum coordinates, ω and h_D have inverse-length units. μ is a mathematical shell parameter.
The Dirac Hilbert pairing is second-variable-linear, with measure d³k/(2π)³. The conjugate space has scalar multiplication z ū = overline(conjugate(z)u) and pairing ⟨ū,v̄⟩=⟨v,u⟩.
At μ=0, k=0, assign complementary rank-two coordinate projections and W_D(t,0)=I. These assignments occur at a Lebesgue-null point; the massless shell apex is omitted.
Spinor Schwartz tests are the finite product of four scalar Schwartz spaces. Spatial Fourier transformation uses exp(−ik·x); u_F integrates W_D(t,k) times that transform. Ψ(F) is antilinear in F.
Particle momenta are q(+,k)=(ω,k), antiparticle momenta are q(−,k)=(ω,−k). Translation phases are exp(i(q⁰a⁰−q⃗·a⃗)); time and spatial generators use U(te₀)=exp(itH) and U(teⱼ)=exp(−itPⱼ).
Covariance is a representation of the explicitly generated triple group with its matrix subspace topology. Tests transform as (S⁻¹)†F(Λ⁻¹(x−a)); cyclicity concerns the global graded field algebra.
The rest-projector example assumes μ>0 and concerns finite-dimensional momentum fibers, not normalizable point-supported continuum states.

load_bearing.statement: Under Countable Choice and the specified scalar-shell and Hilbert-pairing conventions, define the Pauli-block matrices, h_D(k)=α·k+βμ, P±=(I±h_D/ω)/2 off the massless apex, their multiplication ranges, the conjugate negative-energy Hilbert space, and W_D(t,k)=cos(ωt)I+i sin(ωt)h_D/ω.

Assume Countable Choice. For every μ≥0 and almost every k, h_D is Hermitian, h_D²=ω²I, and P± are complementary orthogonal rank-two projections. Their ranges are closed separable Hilbert subspaces; h_D is self-adjoint on {u:ωu∈H_D}. The stated Clifford, spin-lift and W_D identities hold.

Under Countable Choice and the specified Dirac and CAR conventions, u_F depends continuously on Schwartz spinor tests and Ψ(F) is bounded and antilinear. Its CAR scalar is ⟨u_F,u_G⟩; its tested free equation vanishes. The anticommutator kernel is ∂τΔμ I−i h_D(−i∇)Δμ, supported in the closed causal cone, so even polynomials commute across spacelike-separated regions.

Assume Countable Choice and the specified Dirac data. The stated one-particle translation multipliers lift to a strongly continuous fermionic Fock representation. Its joint PVM consists of sector-sum indicator multipliers, supported in the closed future cone; H and P_j have the stated maximal square-integrability domains. The vacuum is the unique zero-energy vector; the nonvacuum energy gap is at least μ when μ>0 and has no positive gap when μ=0.

In a fixed inertial frame, every proper orthochronous linear Lorentz map admits Λ=B_nB(χ)R_nR(θ), with boost and rotation acting by the explicitly stated hyperbolic block and oriented spatial rotation. If Λe₀=e₀, choose χ=0 and R=Λ.

Under Countable Choice and the specified free Dirac data, the explicitly generated triple group projects surjectively onto the proper Poincare group and has a strongly continuous unitary Fock representation implementing the stated test pullback. The vacuum is invariant and cyclic for the global graded algebra; a 2π spin rotation acts as (−1)^N and a 4π rotation as identity. Translation generators and spectrum are those of the fermionic translation lemma.
